Unit 11 • SL

Global Networking

Introduction

How do networks move data reliably and securely at global scale?

This unit develops your understanding of network design, communication rules, addressing, and security controls. You will analyze how systems connect, how protocols coordinate data exchange, and how firewall policies reduce risk.

You will describe network purpose and characteristics, describe transport/application protocols, describe practical topology use, describe IP addressing models, and discuss firewall effectiveness in realistic deployment contexts.

Network types and purpose

Networks are structured by scale, scope, and security needs.

  • PAN/LAN/WAN: personal to global connectivity layers.
  • VPN: secure remote access over public infrastructure.
  • Core goal: reliable communication between distributed systems.

Protocols and communication

Protocols define predictable behavior across different layers.

  • TCP/UDP: transport choices for reliability vs speed.
  • HTTP/HTTPS: web application communication.
  • DHCP: automatic address assignment.

Topology and addressing

Architecture and addressing decisions shape performance and manageability.

  • Topologies: star, mesh, hybrid use different trade-offs.
  • IPv4/IPv6: addressing formats with different scale limits.
  • NAT and private/public ranges: practical internet connectivity model.

Security controls

Firewalls enforce policy but are one layer in a wider security posture.

  • Rule-based filtering by IP, port, and protocol.
  • Protection value depends on rule quality and maintenance.
  • Discussion requires both strengths and limits.

Key Terminology
TermDefinition
LAN / WAN / PAN / VPNNetwork categories defined by geographic scope and communication purpose.
ProtocolSet of communication rules that ensures interoperable data exchange.
TCP / UDPTransport protocols prioritizing reliability/order or low-latency speed.
HTTP / HTTPSWeb protocols; HTTPS provides encrypted secure communication.
DHCPProtocol assigning IP configuration automatically to client devices.
TopologyPhysical or logical arrangement of nodes and links in a network.
IPv4 / IPv6Internet addressing standards using 32-bit and 128-bit addresses.
Static / Dynamic IPFixed manual allocation vs automatically assigned addresses.
NATAddress translation between private local networks and public internet addresses.
FirewallSecurity mechanism that allows or blocks traffic based on policy rules.

Common Misconceptions

WiFi automatically means internet

WiFi provides local wireless connectivity; internet access still depends on routing and upstream service.

TCP and HTTP do the same job

TCP is transport reliability; HTTP/HTTPS are application protocols using transport services.

A firewall alone makes a network secure

Firewalls are essential but must be combined with patching, access control, and endpoint security.

Syllabus Coverage

  • A2.1.1 Network purpose and characteristics
  • A2.1.4 Transport and application protocols
  • A2.2.1 Network topologies
  • A2.3.1 IP addressing
  • A2.4.1 Firewall effectiveness

Real-World Uses

  • School and multi-site campus network planning
  • Secure remote staff access through VPN deployment
  • Protocol selection for reliable vs real-time services
  • Addressing and NAT design for local/private networks
  • Firewall policy design and review

Think Deeper

"How should a network balance openness, performance, and security?" Network design always involves trade-offs between user experience, risk reduction, and operational complexity.
